model.rationale: The district's seventeen-point Republican lean, Jerry Carl's dominant fundraising and outside spending, and market pricing near 95% Republican all point the same way; with no polls contradicting that picture, the open question is the size of the margin, not the winner.
model.watch: Any late general-election polling, a major scandal, or an unusual turnout environment could move the margin, though a Democratic win would require a historic misalignment with the district's fundamentals.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District leans heavily Republican after redistricting, with a partisan lean of roughly seventeen points toward the GOP. The seat is open, and Republican Jerry Carl enters the general election with a decisive financial edge: about $1.2 million raised and more than $547,000 in outside support, against roughly $86,000 for Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. Prediction markets give Carl about a 95% chance of winning.

No general-election polls are available for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. All three point in the same direction. A Democratic win would require a district-wide shift far beyond anything visible in the evidence. The race sits in Safe Republican territory, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
